taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit: a low spring herb with basal leaves and a leafless flowering stalk.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name; wcvp_names.csv of the v16 zip, read 2026-10-17).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Small (1913), Erythronium americanum: the flowering stalk 1 to 3 dm tall, simple.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Small (1913), Erythronium americanum: blades 10 to 15 cm long.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Small (1913), Erythronium americanum: blades oblong to elliptic, pointed, entire, sheathing where they meet the ground; read as oblong and elliptic alike.

traits.perennation.note: Small (1913), Erythronium americanum: lasts from an ovoid corm 1 to 2.5 cm long, new ones formed at the ends of offshoots (the key to the genus).

traits.rosette.note: Small (1913), Erythronium americanum: the leaves seemingly all at the foot, usually two.

traits.inflorescence.note: Small (1913), Erythronium americanum: one flower on a simple stalk, nodding as in the genus.

traits.flower_colour.note: Small (1913), Erythronium americanum: tepals pale to greenish yellow inside, spotted near the base. The colour is our reading of the words.

generator.params.note: Set by hand: a small colony of corm shoots, each with two basal leaves held low and spreading, two shoots in five sending up a leafless stalk with one nodding flower (Small 1913: leaves usually 2, one flower; the one-leaved sterile shoots of a colony are drawn with two). Flower about 4.5 cm across, its tepals 3 to 3.5 cm long and turned back (Small 1913). Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 18 cm to the top of the flowering stalk at 4 years, within Small's 1 to 3 dm stalks (1913). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: grey-green, glossy leaves (Small 1913: lustrous on both faces, commonly mottled above); yellow tepals reflexed, browner at the centre where Small has them spotted within.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.parallel.note: By eye from the same iNaturalist leaf photos: fine veins running the blade's length beside the midrib and meeting at the tip, as in the genus; four each side drawn.

appearance.organs.basal.variegation.note: By eye from research-grade iNaturalist leaf photos (6 to 12 plants, without flowers, read 2026-10-17; for example observation 112742035): brownish-purple blotches, a pigment, over a fifth to a half of the grey-green upper face, soft edged and stretched along the parallel veins, some leaves plain. Drawn as the mottle variegation on the upper face, about a third of the blade on an average leaf, its blotches two and a half times as long as wide along the blade. Small (1913) has the blades commonly mottled above.
